bib.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; figure-only data (Figs 4-12, 14, 15) not extractable as numbers.

question: Can a GPT model fine-tuned on GitHub Python code write functionally correct function bodies from docstrings, and how should that be measured?
hypothesis: A specialized GPT model (Codex) fine-tuned on public code would excel at coding tasks; fine-tuning on a distribution closer to the eval task (standalone functions) should further help.
contributions: Codex: GPT fine-tuned on GitHub Python code (up to 12B parameters)
HumanEval: 164 hand-written problems with unit tests, plus the unbiased pass@k estimator and a sandbox for executing untrusted code
Codex-S (supervised fine-tuning on standalone functions) and Codex-D (docstring generation)
Finding that repeated sampling and log-prob ranking raise solve rates
Limitations and hazard analysis (alignment, bias, security, economics)

method.summary: GPT-3-family models up to 12B were fine-tuned on 159 GB of filtered GitHub Python for 100B tokens to give Codex; further fine-tuned on curated standalone-function problems to give Codex-S, and trained on docstring generation to give Codex-D. Evaluated by functional correctness (pass@k, unbiased estimator, n=200 samples per problem) on the new HumanEval set.
method.task: docstring-to-Python-function synthesis, evaluated by unit tests

datasets.name: GitHub Python corpus (Codex pretraining/fine-tuning)
datasets.size: 179 GB unique Python files under 1 MB, 159 GB after filtering; from 54 million public repositories
datasets.split: held-out split used for test loss (size not stated)
datasets.preprocessing: dropped files likely auto-generated, average line length > 100, max line length > 1000, or small percentage of alphanumeric characters

datasets.name: HumanEval
datasets.size: 164 problems, average 7.7 unit tests per problem
datasets.source: hand-written by authors; released at github.com/openai/human-eval
datasets.preprocessing: each problem has signature, docstring, body, unit tests

datasets.name: Competitive programming problems (Codex-S training)
datasets.source: several programming contest and interview prep websites
datasets.preprocessing: unit tests from examples in statements or extra cases obtained by submitting incorrect solutions

datasets.name: Continuous-integration traced problems (Codex-S training)
datasets.source: GitHub repos using travis and tox plus PyPI packages; inputs/outputs traced with sys.setprofile during integration tests
datasets.preprocessing: filtered by sampling 100 solutions from Codex-12B per problem and dropping problems with no passing sample; verification rerun several times to drop stateful or non-deterministic problems

datasets.name: APPS
datasets.split: test problems used; Codex not fine-tuned on APPS
datasets.preprocessing: 1-shot: one input/output example from the task description appended to the docstring

models.name: Codex
models.init_from: GPT-3 model family (same size); no improvement over training from scratch but converges faster
models.tokenizer: GPT-3 text tokenizer plus extra tokens for whitespace runs (about 30% fewer tokens for code)

models.name: Codex-D
models.architecture: Codex fine-tuned to write docstrings from code

models.name: GPT-Neo (125M, 1.3B, 2.7B)
models.architecture: GPT-style, trained on The Pile (8% GitHub)

training.objective: Codex: next-token (autoregressive) language modelling on code. Codex-S: minimise negative log-likelihood of the reference solution with loss masked on prompt tokens. Codex-D: NLL of the docstring given signature and solution.
training.lr: Codex: same as the corresponding GPT model (value not stated). Codex-S: 1/10 of the Codex fine-tuning learning rate
training.lr_schedule: 175-step linear warmup then cosine decay; Codex-S uses the same schedule
training.tokens: Codex: 100 billion tokens total; Codex-S: until validation loss plateaus, less than 10B tokens
training.compute: Fine-tuning Codex-12B consumed hundreds of petaflop/s-days, similar to the original GPT-3-12B training

other.codex_s_batching: prompts of varying length in a batch are left-padded to the longest so the first reference-solution tokens line up

inference.temperature: tuned per k: Codex pass@1 T*=0.2, pass@100 T*=0.8 (679M model); Codex-S pass@1 T*=0, pass@100 T*=1; Fig 1 and ranking experiments T=0.8; APPS T=0.6; alignment evals T=0.2; Codex-D grading T=0.8; GPT-Neo best of 0.2/0.4/0.8, GPT-J best of 0.2/0.8, TabNine 0.4 (pass@1) and 0.8 (pass@100)
inference.samples: n = 200 samples per task, k <= 100 for HumanEval (unbiased estimator); APPS: 1000 samples per task; Codex-D: 10 hand-graded samples per problem; problem filtering: 100 samples per training problem
inference.prompting: HumanEval prompt = header, signature, docstring (Fig 2); APPS 1-shot appends one input/output example to docstring

parameters.sample_selection_heuristics: highest mean token log-probability beats random; highest sum log-probability can be slightly worse than random; back-translation score P(ground truth docstring | sample) under Codex-D beats random but loses to mean log-prob
parameters.apps_filter: filtered pass@k keeps only samples passing the 3 public task examples

other.sandbox: gVisor container runtime with eBPF firewall rules on Kubernetes

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: generate n >= k samples per task, count c correct (pass all unit tests), estimate 1 - C(n-c,k)/C(n,k), average over problems; n=200, k<=100

metrics.name: APPS raw / filtered pass@k
metrics.definition: strict accuracy on APPS; filtered keeps only samples passing 3 public examples; bracket counts solutions that time out on some test

metrics.name: Docstring pass rate
metrics.definition: hand-graded: docstring correct if it uniquely and accurately specifies the code body; copying the body is not correct

baselines: GPT-Neo 2.7B fine-tuned on APPS (from Hendrycks et al. 2021)
eval.protocol: Unit-test execution in a sandbox; no seeds or confidence intervals reported.

limits: Codex is not sample efficient to train: hundreds of millions of lines of code; a strong CS student would solve a larger fraction than Codex-12B.
Performance falls roughly 2-3x per added chained operation in a docstring, and the model mis-binds operations to variables.
HumanEval is small (164 problems), Python-only, standalone functions at roughly easy-interview difficulty; no confidence intervals or seeds reported.
Training batch size, learning-rate value, context length, layers/width and sequence length are not stated.
Abstract (70.2%), intro/Fig 1 (77.5%) and Table 1 (72.31%) report different pass@100 figures; alignment appendix says 158 problems vs 164 in the main text.
Docstring evaluation is hand-graded on limited samples; the specification-based evaluation framework (Appendix D) is qualitative only, with results deferred to a forthcoming paper.
Bias, security and economics sections are preliminary and qualitative; models are research versions, not the production Copilot model.

def pass_at_k(n, c, k):
    """
    :param n: total number of samples
    :param c: number of correct samples
    :param k: k in pass@$k$
    """
    if n - c < k: return 1.0
    return 1.0 - np.prod(1.0 - k / np.arange(n - c + 1, n + 1))
pass@k := E_problems[ 1 - C(n-c, k) / C(n, k) ]
